Check: Record the exact job identity and intended scope
Evidence to capture: Platform job ID; tenant; site; device or group; requested actor; requested time; maintenance window
Common interpretation: A missing or ambiguous identity makes later evidence impossible to reconcile
Safe next action: Freeze the original record and create a dated evidence copy before changing anything
Escalation trigger: Job identity or target scope cannot be proven

Evidence to capture: Console state; timestamps and time zone; progress; exit code; stdout; stderr; timeout; retries; audit events
Common interpretation: The summary label may hide whether delivery, execution, or result reporting failed
Safe next action: Export or screenshot the original result and retain raw output before retrying
Escalation trigger: Original evidence has already been overwritten or expired

Evidence to capture: Script or component version; content hash; parameters; interpreter; secrets reference; approval record
Common interpretation: A changed script or parameter set can make two runs non-comparable
Safe next action: Pin the version and parameters used by the failed job
Escalation trigger: The executed content cannot be reconstructed

Check: Define success, stop, and rollback conditions
Evidence to capture: Expected endpoint state; validation command; timeout; stop condition; rollback; business impact; escalation owner
Common interpretation: A green console state is not a complete success definition
Safe next action: Write measurable acceptance and rollback criteria before remediation
Escalation trigger: No authorized rollback or success test exists

Check: Confirm current endpoint identity and check-in
Evidence to capture: Tenant; site; durable device identity; agent ID; last check-in; power and network state
Common interpretation: An offline, stale, or mis-enrolled endpoint can leave a valid job pending
Safe next action: Resolve identity and connectivity before changing the script
Escalation trigger: Endpoint ownership or durable identity is disputed

Evidence to capture: Affected and unaffected targets by tenant; site; agent version; OS; policy; network; first-failure time
Common interpretation: A shared boundary often identifies a platform, policy, or environment fault
Safe next action: Narrow the cohort and select one representative canary
Escalation trigger: The failure spans multiple tenants or a rapidly growing cohort

Evidence to capture: Service health; queue depth; concurrency; rate limits; approval state; schedule expiry; maintenance window; cancellation
Common interpretation: The job may be valid but blocked, expired, superseded, or waiting for capacity
Safe next action: Clear only the verified constraint or reschedule one canary
Escalation trigger: Provider degradation or queue failure is suspected

Evidence to capture: Created; queued; delivered; acknowledged; started; completed timestamps and identifiers
Common interpretation: One platform label may collapse several distinct states
Safe next action: Locate the last confirmed state and troubleshoot the next transition
Escalation trigger: The platform cannot expose state-transition evidence

Check: Confirm identity, privilege, and session context
Evidence to capture: Configured account; token or service identity; privilege; session type; user profile; working directory; architecture
Common interpretation: A script can work interactively but fail under a service, SYSTEM, or non-interactive context
Safe next action: Reproduce with the intended bounded context on one canary
Escalation trigger: Required privilege cannot be justified or attributed

Evidence to capture: Application control; EDR; antivirus; signing; execution policy; constrained language; block event IDs
Common interpretation: Security controls may block a child process or file while the RMM reports a generic failure
Safe next action: Create a narrow evidence-backed exception only if authorized; do not disable controls globally
Escalation trigger: Security tooling blocked or quarantined privileged content

Evidence to capture: Files; modules; interpreters; environment variables; registry paths; shares; credentials; certificates; services
Common interpretation: A missing or wrong-version dependency can fail before business logic starts
Safe next action: Repair the narrow dependency and record its version and source
Escalation trigger: A credential, certificate, or privileged dependency is missing

Check: Test network and trust dependencies in the same context
Evidence to capture: DNS; proxy; TLS chain; firewall; repository; package source; destination reachability
Common interpretation: Interactive connectivity does not prove service-context connectivity
Safe next action: Run a read-only connectivity test as the automation identity
Escalation trigger: TLS, proxy, firewall, or third-party service failure affects multiple targets

Evidence to capture: Parent and child processes; scheduled tasks; services; locks; temp files; transcripts; event logs
Common interpretation: The endpoint may show execution that the RMM console did not receive
Safe next action: Build a timestamped local sequence around the job window
Escalation trigger: Privileged child activity is unexplained

Evidence to capture: First local error; platform output; delivery state; interpreter error; script error; timeout; reboot; lost-result evidence
Common interpretation: Later errors are often consequences rather than root cause
Safe next action: Fix the earliest proven boundary first
Escalation trigger: Evidence indicates platform delivery or result-ingestion failure

Check: Review script assumptions and result handling
Evidence to capture: Exit-code logic; exception handling; output encoding; quoting; parameter expansion; current directory; architecture
Common interpretation: The job may report success despite a native-process failure or fail from path and encoding differences
Safe next action: Correct one verified assumption and version the change
Escalation trigger: The script can produce destructive or misleading success states

Check: Determine whether work is active or blocked
Evidence to capture: CPU and I/O activity; child-process state; input prompts; network wait; installer state; reboot request; lock owner
Common interpretation: A long-running job is different from a deadlocked or input-blocked job
Safe next action: Set a bounded observation window and safe termination rule
Escalation trigger: The process exceeds the authorized window or affects production service

Evidence to capture: Resources already changed; repeated side effects; checkpoints; rollback state; duplicate records
Common interpretation: A blind rerun can repeat privileged changes or corrupt state
Safe next action: Inventory partial changes before retry, resume, replacement, or rollback
Escalation trigger: Idempotency is unknown for a high-impact action

Evidence to capture: Change record; actor; script version; dependency or policy change; reason; expected effect
Common interpretation: Multiple simultaneous changes destroy causal evidence
Safe next action: Change one variable and preserve before-and-after evidence
Escalation trigger: The fix requires broad policy or security changes

Evidence to capture: Canary target; bounded privilege; timeout; live output; stop condition; rollback; observer
Common interpretation: A representative canary limits blast radius and tests the actual execution context
Safe next action: Execute once on the approved canary and verify endpoint state independently
Escalation trigger: The canary cannot represent the failing cohort

Check: Prevent unsafe widening and retry loops
Evidence to capture: Target-selection diff; retry count; security exceptions; credential exposure review
Common interpretation: Fleet-wide retries or global control changes can amplify an uncertain failure
Safe next action: Keep the target narrow and require explicit approval before expansion
Escalation trigger: Automation is widening targets or retrying without a hard limit

Evidence to capture: New job ID; target; actor; version; parameters; start and finish times; exit code; output; audit trail
Common interpretation: A corrected run must be independently attributable and reproducible
Safe next action: Attach the complete new job record to the incident or change
Escalation trigger: Audit attribution or result evidence is incomplete

Check: Verify the intended endpoint state independently
Evidence to capture: Configuration; service; file; registry; package; process; telemetry; business-function evidence
Common interpretation: Console success can still leave the endpoint unchanged or partially changed
Safe next action: Run the predeclared acceptance test outside the job summary
Escalation trigger: Business function or security state does not match the intended result

Evidence to capture: Succeeded; failed; pending; offline; excluded; cancelled; unknown; rolled back; owned-exception counts
Common interpretation: Unreconciled targets hide residual risk and future duplicate work
Safe next action: Assign every target one outcome and owner
Escalation trigger: Any privileged or customer-critical target remains unknown

Evidence to capture: Root cause; prevention change; monitoring improvement; residual risk; customer impact; owner; review date
Common interpretation: Closure without prevention and ownership invites recurrence
Safe next action: Publish the bounded lesson and schedule review of exceptions
Escalation trigger: Root cause is unresolved or residual risk lacks an owner
